Not knowing something is not a failure. Saying "I couldn't verify this" or

If you find something, cite it and quote what it actually says - don't
paraphrase a source into numbers it may not contain. If you don't find

Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the search results, here are documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated submissions as a burden.

### Curl (Daniel Stenberg)
Daniel Stenberg, the founder and maintainer of curl, has been vocal about the impact of AI-generated bug reports ("slop") on his project. He initially introduced disclosure requirements in May 2025 and eventually shut down the project's bug bounty program in January 2026 due to the volume of invalid reports.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "We now ban every reporter instantly who submits reports we deem AI slop." | CLAIM: Daniel Stenberg implemented an immediate ban for reporters submitting low-quality AI-generated bug reports.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "The amount of time it takes project maintainers to triage each AI-assisted vulnerability report made via HackerOne, only for them to be deemed invalid, is tantamount to a DDoS attack on the project." | CLAIM: Stenberg compared the time cost of triaging AI bug reports to a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "If we could, we would charge them for this waste of our time." | CLAIM: Stenberg expressed frustration over the uncompensated time lost to verifying bogus AI reports.
SOURCE: https://www.axios.com/2026/03/10/ai-agents-spam-the-volunteers-securing-open-source-software | QUOTE: "The never-ending slop submissions take a serious mental toll to manage and sometimes also a long time to debunk... Time and energy that is completely wasted while also hampering our will to live." | CLAIM: Stenberg described the psychological burden and burnout caused by managing AI spam.
SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "By January 2026, after receiving seven submissions in a sixteen-hour period (some were real bugs; none were actual vulnerabilities), he finally ended the program." | CLAIM: The curl bug bounty program was terminated in January 2026 following a surge of non-vulnerable AI submissions.
SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "My experience of it is that it feels more stupid because it feels more like fighting a machine rather than humans, and that’s just even more tiring and exhausting." | CLAIM: Stenberg noted that dealing with AI bots is more exhausting than dealing with human errors.

### Python (Seth Larson)
Seth Larson, a maintainer for Python, raised concerns about the cost and time required to investigate AI-generated security reports that appear legitimate at first glance.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports." | CLAIM: Seth Larson highlighted the emotional toll and isolation maintainers face when wasting time on bogus security reports.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "All of these feelings can add to burnout of likely highly trusted contributors to open source projects." | CLAIM: Larson warned that AI slop contributes directly to maintainer burnout.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "In many ways, these low-quality reports should be treated as if they are malicious." | CLAIM: Larson suggested treating low-quality AI reports with the same severity as malicious attacks due to their impact.

### Ghostty (Mitchell Hashimoto)
Mitchell Hashimoto, maintainer of Ghostty, shifted from requiring AI disclosure to a zero-tolerance policy for external AI contributions, citing the poor quality of submissions.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "This is not an anti-AI stance. This is an anti-idiot stance." | CLAIM: Hashimoto clarified that his restrictions were aimed at low-effort contributions rather than AI technology itself.
SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "It’s a fucking war zone out here man. Maintainer morale at an all time low." | CLAIM: Hashimoto described the current environment for open-source maintainers as highly stressful and demoralizing.
SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "I totally empathize with the projects that flip the table and ban all AI." | CLAIM: Hashimoto expressed support for other projects choosing to ban AI contributions entirely.

### tldraw (Steve Ruiz)
Steve Ruiz, founder of tldraw, closed external pull requests after being overwhelmed by AI-generated code that lacked genuine engagement or understanding of the project.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "My low-effort issues were becoming low-effort pull requests, with AI doing both sides of the work." | CLAIM: Ruiz observed a cycle where his own AI-assisted issue creation led to AI-assisted, low-quality pull requests from others.
SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "We would get PRs from people who seemed like they put a lot of work into this PR, but they would never reply to sign the contributor license agreement, and it was like, ‘Man, you put all this time into this code, and then, you just never came back to the thread, like, what?’" | CLAIM: Ruiz noted that AI-generated PRs often came from users who did not follow through on basic contribution requirements, indicating a lack of genuine intent.
SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "someone opened up 7 security advisories today all of which did not make sense in the context of our project... all clearly AI generated" | CLAIM: Ruiz reported receiving multiple nonsensical, AI-generated security advisories in a single day.

### RubyGems (Marty Haught)
Marty Haught, director of open source at Ruby Central, discussed the increased volume of reports facing RubyGems.

SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "It takes time, if you get 20 or 50 of these in a week, that could be a full day just reviewing that, where it was maybe 15 minutes previously, and so, now, what do we do?" | CLAIM: Haught illustrated the drastic increase in time required to review bug reports due to AI spam.
SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "RubyGems, the package manager for the Ruby programming language, is mulling a similar move because it hasn’t seen a valid report in months..." | CLAIM: RubyGems considered closing its bug bounty program due to a lack of valid submissions amidst the AI noise.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Direct links to the original Mastodon post by Daniel Stenberg or the specific GitHub issues/tweets by Mitchell Hashimoto and Steve Ruiz mentioned in the aggregators. The provided sources are secondary articles (The Register, Axios, RedMonk, LeadDev) that quote these individuals.
